newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU vets Blokker buy of Toys "R" Us Dutch unit.
newsitem.headline: EU vets Blokker buy of Toys "R" Us Dutch unit.

text.p: The European Commission said on Tuesday it was starting a routine probe into the proposed acquisition of the Dutch subsidiary of U.S. toy retailer Toys "R" Us by Blokker BV of the Netherlands.
The Commission was asked to examine the deal under the merger regulation 4064/89/EEC last year, but in August it stopped its probe because the agreement had not been finalised.

The Commission said in a notice published in the European Union's Official Journal C32 that it was asked to assess the impact of the deal on fair competition by the Dutch authorities under article 22 of the regulation.
Failing that it would have had no competence to carry out the investigation as the deal does not meet the turnover thresholds in the merger regulation.

Such requests are usually made when there are no national rules to assess creation or strengthening of dominant positions, which is the case of the Netherlands, and the government is concerned about a possible threat to competition.

All alliances falling into this category have met with regulatory problems. In 1995 the Commission blocked a Dutch television joint venture obliging the country's powerful TV producer company Endemol, which had teamed up with TV stations RTL and Veronica, to drop the deal.
The Netherlands filed the latest request on January 23. The Commission has one month from that date to clear the acquisition or start an in-depth probe which could last up to four months.
The Dutch parliament is currently discussing a new competition law which contains a section on mergers.
